content:
Rather a number of times recently I've got very frustrated with grind or simp's inability to do sensible things with Bool.xor, stemming to a large degree from the fact that this is just an abbrev for bne.

In the spirit of this I've created an RFC (lean4#13994) with an associated draft PR (lean4#13995), which is aiming to try and fix this and tidy up the simp normal story here somewhat. During the discovery phase of looking at issues, I turned up lean4#10835, which I think this PR is good (if slightly tangential) work towards. I authored all the core changes by hand, but I had AI assistance with the technical stuff involving the grind propagtors - I hope that's acceptable.
I might be missing the point. Why not just have != be the simp normal form and use that?

So a few reasons. Firstly I do think the desire of lean4#10835 for a branchless implementation of Bool.xor is desirable, and you don't get that from !=. Secondly I think they mean semantically distinct things even if they're extensionally the same function. Thirdly I think it's good to have Bool.xor defined at the same time the other fundamental operators are defined. Finally it's more a thing of - there are deductions you can make for != on Bool that are not generalisable to all lawful!=, whereas essentially those deductions are precisely those associated with lawful xor-like operations.

Essentially I think both are fine as a simp normal form - if I had to choose, I would choose xor, but I think it generally serves fine to have them both - because the meaning is distinct.
